events.label: PayPal (PYPL) board formal response to Stripe/Advent $53B bid — board views offer as inadequate; seeking $70+ per Reuters
events.note: Stripe and Advent International jointly bid $60.50/share (~$53B) on July 16; PYPL surged +18%. Board signaled the offer is inadequate per Reuters/SeekingAlpha (July 17 AH). Formal board response at July 20 meeting. Board is weighing price (seeks $70+), financing certainty, and regulatory timeline (DOJ antitrust on Stripe-PayPal). If board issues formal counter-proposal at $68-72: M&A arb spread re-tightens. If board formally rejects outright: PYPL likely retraces toward $55-58 range. Monday gap lower is the base case given Friday AH signal. PayPal's July 28 earnings report becomes the next fundamental read on the core checkout business.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 earnings (AH) + IBM full Q2 earnings call + GOOGL Q2 earnings (AH) — triple clearing event; BEARISH regime context
events.note: The week's defining risk event — now arriving in a BEARISH regime (SPX below 7,460; WTI $82.49 formal breach). TSLA: Q2 follow-on to blowout July 2 delivery report (480K vs 406K); gross margin >25% (from sub-15% in Q1) and FSD revenue recognition are the re-rate gates to above $410. IBM: CEO must clarify whether the enterprise budget rotation is one-quarter or multi-year — that answer drives NOW, CRM, ACN direction. GOOGL: now significantly complicated by (1) Gemini 3.5 Pro months-behind-schedule delay and (2) Moonshot AI Kimi K3 competitive threat at 70% pricing discount to US frontier models. GOOGL must address AI competitive narrative, Search market-share data, and capex trajectory. A weak GOOGL print on any of these dimensions would extend the BEARISH regime. A triple-beat (TSLA margin + IBM one-quarter + GOOGL AI monetization) is the only path to BEARISH → STEP ASIDE re-assessment.

events.label: AMD AI Day (San Francisco, Jul 22-23) — MI400 roadmap vs. NVDA; now must address Moonshot AI Kimi K3 second DeepSeek shock
events.note: AMD's annual AI event in San Francisco runs July 22-23. Context has materially changed from prior brief: AMD fell ~7% on July 17 due to the Moonshot AI Kimi K3 second DeepSeek shock on top of TSMC wafer hike margin pressure. AMD AI Day now must address both simultaneously: (1) MI400 roadmap vs. NVDA H100/Blackwell and (2) GPU cluster inference demand thesis in a world where Chinese open-weight frontier models price at $15/M output tokens vs. $50/M for US equivalents. AMD AI Day closes ($529.14 July 16 → ~$492 July 17) make hyperscaler win disclosures the essential element — competitive pricing or win announcements are the only credible response to the Moonshot AI demand-disruption narrative. UBS PT $700, Rosenblatt $665 on AMD; both may face revision given the Moonshot II shock. Do not add AMD above $495 ahead of the event.

events.label: FOMC meeting (Jul 28-29) — July hike ~33.7%; September hike probability ~69% post-WTI $82 breach; September language is the critical signal
events.note: July hike base case is elevated — CME FedWatch shows ~33.7% probability of a July hike (reversed from 15-20% earlier this week after June CPI 0.0% MoM, as WTI formal $82.49 breach overwhelmed the June CPI relief). September hike probability is now ~69% combined (51% for 25bps + 18% for 50bps), up from 38% at the July 17 morning open and 58% at July 16 close. The September language in the FOMC statement and dot-plot update is the market-moving variable. If Warsh's dot-plot signals September 25bps clearly: 30Y re-accelerates, IWM headwinds worsen, BUY conditions pushed back to post-August CPI. If dots retain September ambiguity: rate relief window opens. Key watch: August 13 July CPI is the primary input; WTI $82.49 settlement and Brent $88.10 will fully load into July energy components — the August CPI oil-shock is structurally embedded.

events.label: META Q2 2026 earnings — AI cloud business quantification; MSFT + AMZN also; peak Q2 earnings week
events.note: META Q2 earnings July 29 is the first event where management must quantify the AI cloud business (Bloomberg July 1: Meta building AI cloud to sell excess compute). MSFT and AMZN also report in late July — peak Q2 earnings risk window. IBM's enterprise software warning (July 14) adds a risk factor for MSFT Azure enterprise consulting revenue. META's ad-driven model is most insulated from Moonshot AI Kimi K3 demand disruption — Chinese open-weight inference disruption primarily threatens GPU cluster spend, not ad-optimization models. GOOGL reports July 22 (earlier, in the triple-event session). PYPL board rejection of Stripe/Advent bid could weigh on fintech sentiment by July 29.

events.label: July CPI release (est. Aug 13) — WTI $82.49 formal breach + Brent $88.10 Hormuz premium fully embedded; most consequential macro print of 2026
events.note: July CPI is the first release to fully capture the WTI formal $82.49 settlement (July 17) and the ongoing Iran Hormuz blockade at 4.1M bpd (62% below pre-crisis norm of 10.8M bpd). Brent at $88.10 on July 17 settlement represents the peak single-day print of the conflict. WTI weekly gain >10% for the week ending July 17 is historically significant. The FOMC is pricing ~69% probability of a September hike as of July 17 close — August CPI is the primary input that will confirm or reverse that pricing. Bull scenario (August CPI <3.2% YoY with oil-shock not embedding in core): September hike probability collapses, BUY conditions open. Bear scenario (August CPI >3.5% YoY with WTI oil-shock passing through to services/transportation): September 50bps probability jumps, BEARISH regime extends. June CPI 0.0% MoM demonstrated that prior oil shocks did not embed; the July shock magnitude ($82.49, +10% weekly) is larger.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — $91B revenue guide; AI capex cycle clearing event; now must address Moonshot AI demand disruption
events.note: NVDA's Q2 FY27 earnings is the fundamental clearing event for the AI capex thesis. $91B revenue guidance represents sequential acceleration. TSMC Q2 (July 16) confirmed AI demand thesis with supply shortage for N3/N5 nodes extending into 2027. However, three new risk factors exist vs. prior NVDA brief: (1) TSMC 5-10% wafer price hike across 74% of wafer revenue = 2-4pp gross margin headwind management must quantify; (2) Moonshot AI Kimi K3 (July 17) is a frontier-class open-weight model at 70% pricing discount that challenges hyperscaler GPU cluster inference demand; (3) September hike probability at ~69% applies a discount-rate headwind to NVDA's 37x forward multiple. NVDA held the $195 hard stop through the July 14-17 selloff — the stock's relative strength despite AMD –7%, GOOGL –4.4% on July 17 is notable. Full-size add gate: sustained close above $210 + wafer hike impact clarified + Moonshot AI demand impact quantified + VIX below 15.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since June 12 IPO. SPCX touched an intraday all-time low of $132.75 on July 15 (below $135 IPO price) — down 30%+ from June 16 ATH of $225.64. 27 of 31 analysts still carry Buy ratings; the sell-side downgrade cycle has barely begun. December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang. Re-entry gate: first earnings print (Starlink ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn) is the fundamental clearing event. Net losses are structural ($4.9B in 2025, $4.28B in Q1 2026). Better entry $115-120 for risk-tolerant 12-month investors.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs. The $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories.
